Spread is a judgement, not a published variance: CL gsd 1.35 covers the elderly-vs-young clearance difference 19 vs 25 L/h (Abernethy 1990).

Apparent parameters for rhein after oral diacerein, which is entirely converted to rhein (Nicolas 1998): CL/F 1.6 L/h and t1/2 4.3 h (Magnard 1993), so V/F = CL/F * t1/2 / ln2 = 9.93 L; F is set to 1 because the parameters are already apparent. ka 1.5 per h is an assumption (no verified Tmax for rhein), hence the wide ka spread. Rhein is about 99 percent protein bound (Nicolas 1998).
